scope: T1c finite classical Hamiltonian-constraint diagnostic; no full GR/QG, measurement, arrow, or phenomenology claim.

PITR_interpretation.P2: phi is globally monotonic in the stipulated solution; alpha and beta turn repeatedly.
PITR_interpretation.P4: fixed record coupling produces nonzero quantified alpha backreaction.
PITR_interpretation.P5: the fixed pointers physically record alpha/beta more directly than phi, but do not convert a turning alpha into a global clock.
PITR_interpretation.P6: alpha-to-beta canonical relabelling preserves turnings and record mutual information up to numerical binning.
PITR_interpretation.combined_selection_result: PITR adds no independent clock selection in this model beyond monotonicity/domain plus the stipulated interaction choice.

conclusion: The record bank is interaction-relative: it can robustly correlate with a turning geometric variable. Public records alone therefore do not make that variable a global physical clock. In this model PITR does not yet improve on ordinary monotonicity/domain analysis.
